samples.summary: The live slides read boundary bands table cell bodies but leaves the table element's `data.columnWidths` uncapped — the unbounded `nCols` allocation this change caps on every other path
samples.evidence:
`bandElementText` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:528-543) is the band on the collaborative path the design doc names as the one that matters ("nothing stops a collaborator calling `doc.update`"). Its table branch is `if (type !== 'table' || !Array.isArray(record.rows)) return;` followed by a walk of `rows[].cells[].body.blocks` only — `record.columnWidths` is never touched.

The identical shape IS capped everywhere else the change touches: the backend `PUT` caps it at `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:965-967, `data.columnWidths.slice(0, MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS)`), and `bandTableColumnWidths` in packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:73-76 does the same for the snapshot-adapter / backend-slide-op path. The one reader that actually serves the live editor does not.

Sink, confirmed: packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:87-92 — `const nCols = columnWidths.length; const colX = new Array(nCols + 1); for (let c = 0; c < nCols; c++) ...`, and line 41 `const nCols = data.columnWidths.length` drives the `for (r) for (c)` cell loop in `drawTable`.

Attack: any workspace member (or any holder of a write-scoped API key who then edits through the frontend) calls `doc.update` writing a table element with `data.columnWidths` of ~1e6 numeric entries — a few MB of CRDT, well under any limit. `YorkieSlidesStore.read()` hands it through unaltered, and every *other* viewer's next paint allocates `nCols + 1` offsets and loops `rows.length * 1e6` times per frame: a hung tab for everybody but the attacker. This is precisely the denial of service the rest of the change exists to close, left open on the primary path.

samples.summary: `bandBlockNumerics` fails OPEN at `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` — a nested-table chain one level deeper than the cap keeps an unbanded `rowSpan`, which `expandCellRangeForMerges` turns into a ~1e9-iteration loop for every viewer

`bandOneBlock` descends into a cell's blocks only while `depth < MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` (32) and otherwise silently leaves everything below "as stored" (the module comment at packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:98-111 states this is deliberate). The consumers the band protects have no matching cap: `treeNodeToBlock`/`treeNodeToCell` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts) recurse nested tables without bound, and so does the layout walk.

Sink, confirmed by reading it: packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:66-91 — `while (changed) { for (let r = rowStart; r <= rowEnd; r++) ... const r2 = r + rspan - 1; if (r2 > rowEnd) { rowEnd = r2; changed = true; } }`. samples.summary: `bandElementNumerics` stops descending at `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` while `flattenElements` and the renderer recurse groups without a cap — 33 nested groups defeat the band entirely on the revision-preview and backend slide-op paths
samples.evidence:
packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:112 — `if (el.type === 'group' && depth < MAX_GROUP_DEPTH)`. Past depth 32 the walk returns the element untouched, banding nothing below it and raising nothing.

samples.summary: An attacker-controlled JSON object key is interpolated verbatim into a 400 error message — unbounded length and unescaped control characters/newlines, enabling log forging and response amplification
samples.evidence:
`bandMasterPlaceholderStyles` builds `const slotPath = `${path}.placeholderStyles.${slot}`` (line 619) where `slot` comes from `Object.entries(styles)` on `body.masters[i].placeholderStyles` — i.e. an arbitrary key name taken straight off the request body — and then throws `new BadRequestException(`Invalid master at ${slotPath}: '${field}' must be a number`)` (lines 624-626).

Every other error message in this file interpolates only loop indices and fixed field names (`assertValidBlockStyle`, `assertValidSlide`, `normalizeSlideInlines`), and `emptyElementData` goes out of its way to route an untrusted `type` through a `Map` "so the untrusted `type` string can never reach a prototype key" (line 911). This is the first attacker-supplied *string* reflected into an exception message here.

Vector: `PUT` a deck with `masters: [{ placeholderStyles: { "x\nERROR fake-log-line": { fontSize: "1" } } }]`. The non-number `fontSize` forces the throw, and the key — newlines and all — lands in the exception message. If the message reaches the application log (Nest's default exception filter and most log pipelines record it), the attacker writes arbitrary lines into it. The same key can be megabytes long, amplifying both the 400 response body and the log entry. Cheap fix: cap and escape `slot`, or report the slot by index only.
searchedFor: read bandMasterPlaceholderStyles and compared against every other BadRequestException message in docs-content.controller.ts
checked emptyElementData's Map-based guard as the file's own precedent for untrusted keys

samples.summary: An `inline.style.image` stored as an array bypasses `isPaintableImageSize` on both the write band and the read band, so an unpaintable size still reaches the layout engine
samples.evidence:
Write band: `const image = style.image; if (image && typeof image === 'object' && !Array.isArray(image)) { ... isPaintableImageSize(...) ... }` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1332-1343). An array is excluded by `!Array.isArray`, so it is neither banded nor rejected — it is stored.

Read band: `bandOneBlock` does `const image = asRecord(inlineStyle.image); if (image && !isPaintableImageSize(...)) delete inlineStyle.image;` — `asRecord` (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts) returns `undefined` for arrays, so the `delete` never runs there either.

Sink: packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:910-911 — `if (inline.style.image) { const image = inline.style.image; ... }` and :726-732 `seg.image.width` / `seg.image.height`. An array is truthy, so `width`/`height` read as `undefined` and every downstream multiplication yields `NaN` line geometry for every viewer of the stored deck.

Vector: `PUT` (or `doc.update`) a slide text body with `inlines: [{ text: "x", style: { image: [1, 2] } }]`. Both new guards skip it. The paginator's fragment bound keeps this from hanging, so the impact is NaN/blank geometry rather than a hang — but it is a hole in a guard that was added specifically to make this class of value unreachable.
searchedFor: read normalizeSlideInlines image branch and bandOneBlock's inline image branch
read asRecord in packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts
grep style.image / .image in packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts to confirm the consumer dereferences without an Array check

samples.summary: `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` bounds fragments per row only; the total page / `PageLine` allocation across rows stays unbounded, so a many-row table still multiplies into an OOM for every reader
samples.evidence:
The new bound is `if (++fragments >= MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN) fragHeight = remaining;` inside the per-row fragment loop, so it caps one row at 200 pages. Nothing caps the product across rows.

Even with every value banded, `MAX_FONT_SIZE` is 4000 pt (~5333 px per line), so a cell whose content sits at the ceiling legitimately reaches the 200-fragment cap. A peer-written table with a few thousand such rows — a small CRDT payload, since the poison is one attribute per row — therefore asks for hundreds of thousands of pages, each carrying its own `PageLine` objects: an OOM or a multi-minute freeze for every reader, from one writer.

I could not confirm a concrete row count that tips a browser over, which is why confidence is low; the structural point is that the bound is per-row and the design doc (`docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-row-splitting.md` §1.5) states the termination guarantee without noting that the aggregate is still unbounded.

finding.summary: `POST .../slides` seeds placeholder blocks from an unbanded master, writing out-of-band typography into the CRDT — bypassing the master band this change adds
finding.evidence:
`apply()` calls `op(readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot()))`, and `readSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:52) applies no band at all. `slide-ops.addSlide` hands that document to `new MemSlidesStore(document)`, whose `addSlide` seeds `blocks: seedPlaceholderBlocks(placeholderStyle, theme)` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:210) and then the controller `splice`s the resulting slide onto the live `root.slides`.

The frontend equivalent bands at exactly this point and says why: yorkie-slides-store.ts:1318-1324 — "this is the reader that actually feeds `seedPlaceholderBlocks`: without it a poisoned master's `fontSize` is *committed* to the CRDT inside the blocks a layout change seeds, where a later read band would only hide it from this client." The backend copy of that path has no `bandMasterNumerics` call.

Attack: a collaborator (or an earlier `PUT` made before this branch) writes `masters[0].placeholderStyles.body.fontSize = 1e9` via `doc.update`. Any workspace member then calls `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/slides` with a `title-body` layout. The seeded blocks are persisted with `fontSize: 1e9`, which is now stored content rather than a per-reader artefact. The new write-side band in `assertValidSlidesBody` (`bandMasterPlaceholderStyles`) does not run on this route, and the read-side band only hides the value from clients that happen to re-band.

verdict.reason: The finding's central evidence is not present in the repository. `apply()` in packages/backend/src/api/v1/slides.controller.ts:187-189 does NOT call `op(readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot()))`; it calls `op(bandSlidesDocumentNumerics(readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot())))`, with `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics` imported at line 36. That function (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:208-230) iterates `root.masters` and calls `bandMasterNumerics` on each (line 227), which clamps every `placeholderStyles[*]` fontSize/lineHeight via `bandPlaceholderStyleNumerics` (lines 158-200), and also bands `root.layouts` (line 224). The seeding sink is fed from that same banded object: slide-ops.addSlide constructs `new MemSlidesStore(document)` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slide-ops.ts:162) with the banded document, and MemSlidesStore.addSlide reads `this.doc.masters` / `master.placeholderStyles[ref.type]` immediately before `seedPlaceholderBlocks(placeholderStyle, theme)` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:181-210). So a poisoned `fontSize: 1e9` is clamped before it can be committed into the blocks spliced onto `root.slides`; the claimed attack chain cannot complete. The only unbanded `readSlidesRoot` call sites are read-only response paths (slides.controller.ts:90 with syncMode 'readonly', docs-content.controller.ts:158), neither of which seeds blocks or writes to the CRDT.

finding.summary: The new MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS / normalizeColumnRatio band is bypassable through a slides `table` element's `data.columnWidths`, which is capped on neither write nor read
finding.evidence:
`bandSlideBlockNumerics` (docs-content.controller.ts:1120-1128) newly caps a docs *block* table's `columnWidths` to `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` (256) and maps every entry through `normalizeColumnRatio`, and `parseColumnWidthsAttr` does the same on the CRDT read side. The sibling shape — a slides *element* of `type: 'table'` — gets neither.

Write side: `assertValidTableData` (line 946) only checks `columnWidths` is an array; no length cap, no per-entry band. Read side: `bandElementNumerics` for `el.type === 'table'` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:72-83) walks only `data.rows[].cells[].body.blocks` and never touches `data.columnWidths` or `rows[].height`.

Sink: `computeTableLayout` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:86-99) sets `nCols = columnWidths.length` and runs `for r in nRows { for c in nCols }`, and `colX[c+1] = colX[c] + columnWidths[c]`. So a `PUT /content` body carrying a `table` element with ~2M `columnWidths` entries (≈12 MB, inside the 25 MB `JSON_BODY_LIMIT`) and 1000 rows produces ~2e9 iterations per layout pass for *every* viewer of the deck, and a single `Infinity`/`-1e400` entry produces NaN cumulative offsets that blank the table. This is the same amplification and the same NaN-geometry outcome the change explicitly bands for the docs-block twin, reached through the path the band skipped.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the slides `table` element's `data.columnWidths` is capped "on neither write nor read", and cites two specific locations as lacking the cap. Both citations are contradicted by the code at those exact lines. WRITE SIDE: `assertValidTableData` does not "only check columnWidths is an array" — packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:953-967 has an `else` branch that rewrites `data.columnWidths = (widths as unknown[]).slice(0, MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS).map((width) => Math.max(0, asFiniteNumber(width) ?? 0))`, with a comment naming `computeTableLayout`'s nCols amplification as the reason. So the described exploit — a PUT /content body with ~2M columnWidths entries inside JSON_BODY_LIMIT — is truncated to 256 entries before storage, and an Infinity/-1e400 entry is coerced to 0, so no NaN reaches colX's running sum. READ SIDE: `bandElementNumerics`'s `el.type === 'table'` branch calls `bandTableColumnWidths(data)` as its first statement (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:100) before walking rows/cells/body.blocks; `bandTableColumnWidths` (lines 72-77) applies the identical slice-to-MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS plus finite/non-negative coercion, and its docstring (lines 53-71) explicitly calls itself the docs-block cap's "twin for the slides *element* shape". A regression test pins it at packages/slides/test/model/band-numerics.test.ts:122-142. That band reaches element-shape readers through bandSlidesDocumentNumerics (band-numerics.ts:216) from slides.controller.ts:188, snapshot-adapters.ts:53/75 and yorkie-board-store.ts:442. Noted but not exculpatory-relevant: the live YorkieSlidesStore.read() uses its own local `bandElementText` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:528-540) which bands only text bodies and does not call bandElementNumerics — that is a different file and a different claim, already tracked separately, and it does not make the two assertions in THIS finding true.

mergedFrom.summary: The new recursion depth cap covers only elements and blocks; `themes`, `guides`, slide `background`, and the `data` of unrecognised element types still reach Yorkie with unbounded nesting

finding.summary: The slides PUT validator's nested-block walk recurses without a depth cap (`assertValidSlideBlocks` → `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` → `assertValidSlideBlocks` through `tableData.rows[].cells[]`), while the sibling element walk in the same file caps at 32 citing exactly this stack-exhaustion risk on this authenticated endpoint.
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks(blocks, path)` (line 1084) takes no `depth` parameter; at line 1135 it calls `assertValidTextBodyBlocks(cell, cellPath)` which calls back into `assertValidSlideBlocks` (line 998) for the cell's own `blocks`, unbounded. The same file justifies `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` at line 729-735 with 'the walk recurses through `data.children` and the JSON body limit is 25 MB — enough for a compact payload to exhaust the stack on an authenticated endpoint' — the identical argument applies here, and to `assertValidBlock` (line 437, recursing into `cell.blocks` at line 478). One nested-table level costs ~50 bytes, so ~50k levels (≈2.5 MB, far under the body limit) is a `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` thrown from inside `PUT /content`. The newly added `bandSlideBlockNumerics`/`bandSlideCellNumerics` calls sit on this same unbounded walk, so the hardening inherits the gap instead of closing it.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing depth cap is present. `assertValidSlideBlocks` is declared with `depth = 0` (docs-content.controller.ts:1175-1178) and guards `if (depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH) throw new BadRequestException('...nested too deeply')` at :1180-1184, propagating `depth + 1` into the table-cell recursion at :1235. Its mutual-recursion partner `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` also takes and threads `depth` (:1070-1074, :1085), so the cycle cannot reset the counter. The docs-arm walk the finding also names, `assertValidBlock`, is likewise capped (:438, :443-447, :488-492), and the comment at :798-806 documents MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH=32 as the shared ceiling for both walks. Dedicated regression tests exercise the exact attack (20000-level nested tables, ~1 MB, far under the 25 MB limit) and assert a 400 `/nested too deeply/` for the slide text body, slide notes, and docs body at docs-content.validation.spec.ts:82-113. The finding's cited line numbers (1084, 998, 437/478) do not match the current file, indicating it was based on a stale revision. Both entry points into the slide walk (:742 notes, :862 data) start at depth 0 and descend under the cap, so there is no unguarded path.
